name: Eyemaxxing

card.summary: Umbrella term for improving the eye area (brows, lashes, eyelid exposure, under-eye skin and eye colour) so the eyes read as more open, alert and defined.
card.note: Ranges from grooming and skincare to eyelid surgery; the surgical end carries medical risks.

quick.overview:
Eyemaxxing is the looksmaxxing term for working on the eye area as a whole. It covers eyebrow shape and grooming, lashes, how much upper eyelid is visible, the skin under the eyes, and sometimes eye colour. The appearance payoff people describe is eyes that look more open, alert and defined, which many in the community treat as a central part of facial attractiveness.

Practitioners describe a ladder of options: lifestyle and skincare basics first, then makeup-style tools such as brow filling and tinting, and at the far end procedures such as canthoplasty or eyelid surgery. Community guides organise the topic this way, from skincare to surgery. Research on individual techniques exists in dermatology and plastic surgery, but eyemaxxing as a package has not been studied.
quick.how: In practice people start with the eye area basics discussed in forum guides: sleep and skincare for under-eye skin, brow grooming, shaping, filling or tinting, and lash care. Some move on to cosmetic procedures performed by clinicians. Results from grooming are immediate; skincare changes are gradual.
quick.risks: Non-surgical steps carry ordinary skin-irritation risks near the eye. Surgical options such as canthoplasty or blepharoplasty carry the usual surgical risks, including infection, asymmetry and effects on eye function, and are performed by qualified surgeons. A forum thread titled around visiting an eye doctor after eyemaxxing shows members also discuss eye-health checks.

lead: Eyemaxxing is a looksmaxxing term for improving the appearance of the eye area, including the brows, lashes, the amount of visible upper eyelid, under-eye skin and, in some discussions, eye colour. Its aim is eyes that look more open, alert and defined, which community members regard as a major contributor to overall facial attractiveness.[1]

Forum guides present eyemaxxing as a progression. One widely shared guide on looksmax.org is titled as running "from skincare to surgery", beginning with lifestyle and skincare foundations (sleep, stress, nutrition, sun protection and topical products), moving through in-office treatments such as peels, microneedling, lasers, injectables and lash and brow enhancement, and ending with eyelid surgery, brow lifts, canthoplasty and ptosis repair.[1] Other threads collect methods for different budgets, for particular eye shapes and for adolescents.[2][3][6]

The vocabulary of eyemaxxing overlaps with the wider looksmaxxing lexicon: "hunter eyes" describes a positive canthal tilt with little upper eyelid exposure and low-set brows, and "prey eyes" describes a neutral or negative tilt.[13][14] Published studies have examined related features, including the tilt of the inner eye corner, orbital measurements in attractive faces and the dark limbal ring around the iris.[15][16] Eyebrow grooming has a long cultural history, and surgical eye-area procedures such as blepharoplasty and canthoplasty are established in plastic surgery.[4][5][9] Eyemaxxing as a combined programme has no studies of its own.

chain: Groom brows, care for lids and under-eye skin
Eye area looks more open and defined
Face reads as more alert and attractive
angle.text: People use eyemaxxing steps such as brow shaping and tinting, lash care and under-eye skincare to change how open and defined the eyes look. Those who pursue surgery aim to alter eyelid or canthal position. Effects of grooming are visible immediately.

paras: Eyemaxxing groups together everything that changes how the eyes and their surroundings look: eyebrow shape and position, lash length and density, how much of the upper eyelid shows, the colour and texture of the skin under the eyes, the tilt of the eye corners, and in some threads eye or iris colour.[1][2] The shared aim is a look that members describe as open, alert and defined rather than tired or droopy.

Forum guides usually arrange the options by invasiveness. A widely read 2025 guide on looksmax.org divides them into "softmaxxing" (lifestyle and skincare foundations, including sleep and stress management, nutrition and supplements, sun protection and targeted topical products), in-office non-surgical treatments (chemical peels and peptides, microneedling with or without platelet-rich plasma, laser and light therapies, Botox and fillers, and lash and brow enhancements) and surgical rejuvenation (upper and lower eyelid blepharoplasty, brow lift, canthoplasty or canthopexy, and ptosis repair).[1] Other thread titles show the same range, from a non-surgical guide to a budget guide to one aimed at people still in puberty.[3][6][23]

Looksmaxxing communities describe a positive canthal tilt, meaning the outer corner of the eye sits higher than the inner corner, as "hunter eyes", and a neutral or negative tilt as "prey eyes". Know Your Meme calls the metric speculative and traces the phrase "canthal tilt" to 4chan boards in 2012 and 2013, spreading through incel forums before TikTok humour and a popular filter in 2023.[13] Wikipedia's looksmaxxing article defines hunter eyes as a positive canthal tilt with little to no upper eyelid exposure and low-set eyebrows, and notes that some practitioners rub the orbital area in an attempt to reach these features alongside mewing or surgery.[14]

Anatomically, the canthus is the corner where the upper and lower eyelids meet, with a medial (inner) and lateral (outer) canthus; canthoplasty is plastic surgery on either corner and is used for both cosmetic and functional eyelid problems.[5] A separate thread asks how much training or rubbing can realistically change the eye area; one reply says the only realistic options are orbicularis oculi training or surgery, and that training will not change the area dramatically.[7]

General reference sources list brow techniques including tweezing, waxing, threading, filling with pencils or powders, tinting, microblading, transplant and brow lifts, and trace brow fashion from Japanese hikimayu to the thin brows of the 1920s.[4] Eyebrows are thought to matter for expression and recognition.[4]

For lashes, reference sources note that extensions, false lashes, tints, curlers and growth products are used to enhance length, and that Allergan introduced bimatoprost solution (Latisse) in the first quarter of 2009 as the first FDA-approved drug for eyelash growth, with the company reporting visible growth within about 16 weeks and up to a 25 percent increase in length.[11] The same source notes that constant pulling of lashes can cause permanent damage.[11]

Dark circles under the eyes have several recognised contributors: heredity, thin lower-eyelid skin that shows underlying vessels, extra pigment, venous congestion, allergy and eye rubbing, sleep loss, age-related thinning and fat descent, and sun exposure.[12] Treatments described in general references include topical products (caffeine, vitamin C), laser and intense pulsed light, fat transfer and hyaluronic acid filler; hydroquinone lost US over-the-counter approval in 2006.[12] Forum guides cover under-eye skincare as part of their foundations tier.[1]

Blepharoplasty is eyelid surgery that removes or repositions excess skin and fat and reinforces supporting tissue; the Roman writer Celsus described cutting away eyelid skin in the first century, and Karl Ferdinand von Graefe coined the term in 1818.[9] Upper blepharoplasty is placed in the natural crease and may be cosmetic or used to restore vision blocked by drooping skin; lower blepharoplasty is done through the skin or from inside the lid; East Asian blepharoplasty creates a supratarsal fold, the "double eyelid".[9] Canthopexy or canthoplasty is sometimes added to stabilise the outer corner and may reduce the risk of postoperative eyelid malposition.[9]

The epicanthic fold, a skin fold that can cover the inner corner of the eye, is common among East Asian and several other populations, and epicanthoplasty is the surgical modification of it.[10] A looksmax.org thread discusses eyemaxxing specifically for Asian eyes.[20]

sections.h: Research on the eye area and attractiveness
paras: A 2007 study in Ophthalmic Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery by Bashour and Geist asked judges to choose between original female faces and versions in which the medial canthal tilt had been exaggerated digitally; the altered faces were preferred 93 percent of the time, and the authors suggested the cue may relate to youthful and sex-typical eyelid angles.[15] A 2015 Angle Orthodontist study measured 199 healthy young adults and 126 participants from beauty competitions aged 18 to 30 with 3D digitisers; the attractive group had a narrower distance between the inner eye corners, longer eye openings and larger eye-opening angles, and the authors proposed the values as references for surgical planning.[15]

Limbal rings, the dark band around the iris, have also been studied. A 2011 study by Peshek and colleagues at the University of California, Irvine showed volunteers 80 pairs of faces identical except for a dark limbal ring, and faces with the ring were rated more attractive; the ring also helped in inverted faces, which the authors read as local feature processing.[16] Evolutionary psychologist Robert Burriss summarised the work and follow-up research in Psychology Today in 2017, noting that rings fade with age, that a Southern Mississippi study found darker rings made faces look healthier with effects depending on the sex of face and rater, and that context such as short-term versus long-term mating changed how rings were valued.[17] The same article reports links between whiter sclera and ratings of health and attractiveness.[17]

Eye-area threads appear across years of looksmax.org history, including early posts on general eyemaxxing, a thread about the work of a user called Taban, a self-described bible and numerous guides.[21][24][25] Wikipedia's looksmaxxing article traces the broader movement to incel message boards in the 2010s and PSL forums before TikTok popularisation in the 2020s, and lists Vice's June 2023 piece on the "hunter eyes" trend among media coverage of the movement.[14] Know Your Meme reports that canthal tilt memes drew millions of plays on TikTok in 2023, including humorous videos and a filter.[13]

Thread titles show the range of audiences: a thread about eyemaxxing during puberty, another about instantly making dark eyes look better, and one asking which eyemaxxing steps gave the most noticeable results.[3][18][19] A teenage poster asks whether anything can improve the upper eye area short of surgery, and replies are mostly jokes, illustrating how younger members discuss the subject.[26]

Some members question how much changes. A thread asks whether eyemaxxing beyond lashes and brows can alter how the eyes look over time, and a reply says only orbicularis oculi training or surgery are realistic.[7] Another thread records a member going to an eye doctor after trying eye-area changes.[8] Guide authors, by contrast, open with a section on why the eye area matters and present the staged ladder as available at any budget.[1][6]

Grooming and skincare near the eye carry ordinary risks of irritation or allergy. Eyelid surgery is described in references as outpatient surgery with swelling and bruising that usually resolve over several weeks, and canthal procedures are used to lower the risk of eyelid malposition after blepharoplasty.[9] Guides on looksmax.org carry disclaimers that the author takes no responsibility for adverse effects and that the content is not medical advice.[1]

No studies found on eyemaxxing as a package. Individual elements such as canthoplasty, blepharoplasty and eyelash growth appear in plastic-surgery and dermatology literature, and attractiveness studies have examined canthal tilt, orbital measurements and limbal rings as described above.[9][11][15][16]

timeline.event: Celsus describes cutting away eyelid skin in De Medicina.[9]
Karl Ferdinand von Graefe coins the term blepharoplasty.[9]
Bashour and Geist report that faces with exaggerated medial canthal tilt were preferred 93 percent of the time.[15]
Bimatoprost solution introduced as the first FDA-approved eyelash growth drug.[11]
Peshek and colleagues report that dark limbal rings raise attractiveness ratings.[16]
Early mentions of canthal tilt on 4chan boards.[13]
Angle Orthodontist study compares orbital measurements of attractive and typical young adults.[15]
Canthal tilt and hunter eyes spread on TikTok; Vice covers the hunter eyes trend in June.[13][14]
A looksmax.org guide lays out eyemaxxing from skincare to surgery.[1]

lore.intro: Eyemaxxing is discussed on looksmax.org in guides and debate threads about how much the eye area matters and which methods change it.[1][7]

claims.claim: The eye area is a major driver of facial attractiveness, so improving it gives outsized results.
claims.believers: Guide authors open with "why the eye area matters" and rank eye-area work highly.[1]
claims.experts: Research examines the eyes among many features, including eye-corner tilt and limbal rings, but no study has tested an eyemaxxing programme.[15][16]

claims.claim: A positive canthal tilt (hunter eyes) is more attractive than a negative one.
claims.believers: Members use the terms hunter eyes and prey eyes as shorthand for attractive and less attractive eye shapes.[13][14]
claims.experts: A 2007 study found digitally increased medial canthal tilt preferred in female faces 93 percent of the time, and a 2015 study found attractive participants had larger eye-opening angles; Know Your Meme notes the 2007 study assessed only female faces.[13][15]

claims.claim: Rubbing or pulling the eye corners can reshape the eye area.
claims.believers: Some practitioners rub the orbital area to try to reach hunter-eye features, and a TikTok video promoted regularly pulling the eye corners upward.[14]
claims.experts: A forum reply says only orbicularis oculi training or surgery are realistic options and that training will not change the eye area dramatically; no published study tests rubbing or pulling.[7]

claims.claim: A dark limbal ring makes eyes more attractive.
claims.believers: Dark-eye and eye-colour threads treat contrast around the iris as a goal.[18]
claims.experts: A 2011 study found faces with dark limbal rings rated more attractive, and later work reported rings raised perceived health with effects depending on rater and context.[16][17]

claims.claim: A staged approach from skincare to surgery lets people improve the eyes at any budget.
claims.believers: Threads on cheap and non-surgical eyemaxxing collect low-cost options.[6][23]
claims.experts: Brow grooming methods, eyelash growth products and eyelid surgery are established cosmetic practices; combined outcomes are not studied.[4][9][11]

claims.claim: Under-eye dark circles can be reduced with skincare and procedures.
claims.believers: Guides place under-eye topical care in their foundation tier.[1]
claims.experts: General references list topical, laser, filler and fat-transfer approaches and describe several causes, including heredity and anatomy.[12]
